item.title: Trump Cancels Rallies, Switches to Remote Midterm Campaigning
item.description: President Donald Trump canceled appearances in Kansas and Iowa for the closing days of the midterm election season, and will instead hold “a large number of tele-rallies,” the Republican National Committee announced on Thursday evening.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Erik Wasson

item.title: Early Voting Turnout Surges Nationwide
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) says the US should “demolish” Iran’s regime and argues the country must prepare for war to achieve peace and prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Patrick McHenry, former House Financial Services Committee chair and Bloomberg contributor, says Democrats are likely to win control of the House, though the size of their majority remains uncertain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: How Democratic Control Could Reshuffle Congress' Most Powerful Committees
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mario Parker joined the show to discuss how Democratic control of Congress could reshape oversight of Wall Street, AI and cryptocurrency. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Government to Scale Back Gasoline Subsidies From December
item.description: Japan plans to gradually scale back gasoline subsidies from December into early spring, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said, adding that support for electricity and gas bills, which was also provided from January through March this year, will be brought forward and begin in December.
item.dc:creator: Akemi Terukina

item.title: Trump on Alaska Sen. Race Controversy: It's Voter Fraud
item.description: Bloomberg’s Anna Edgerton joined the show to discuss the Alaska Senate race and the potential legal and campaign-finance questions surrounding ballot stacking. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McHenry Sees Democratic House, GOP Leadership Fight
item.description: Patrick McHenry, former House Financial Services Committee chair and Bloomberg contributor, says Democrats are likely to win control of the House, though the size of their majority remains uncertain. McHenry says a Republican loss could set up a leadership battle between Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise, with Scalise’s existing leadership infrastructure potentially giving him an advantage. McHenry says Hakeem Jeffries could face a difficult task managing Democrats even if he becomes speaker, particularly with a narrow majority and ideological divisions inside the caucus. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Scott Says US Should ‘Demolish’ Iran’s Regime
item.description: Sen. Scott (R-FL) says the US should “demolish” Iran’s regime and argues the country must prepare for war to achieve peace and prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Sen. Scott says the US military has the capability to bring the conflict to a conclusion rather than continue costly operations protecting oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Sen. Scott says he opposes government grants to companies but would prefer taxpayers receive equity when federal money is provided, arguing the government should seek a return on those investments. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Amazon Chip Earnings (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Amazon reported higher capital spending than expected, while its e-commerce revenue slowed ahead of a potentially lukewarm holiday sales season. Intel's revenue forecast missed estimates, hurt by sputtering demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems with its lucrative data center companies.
On today's episode:
Kunjan Sobhani, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Semiconductor Analyst Anurag Rana, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Tech Analyst Jake Silverman, Bloomberg Intelligence Semiconductor Analyst Liz Ann Sonders, Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Mike Townsend, Schwab Managing Director of Legislative & Regulatory Affairs (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 1789 Capital’s Paul Abrahimzadeh on IPO Market Outlook
item.description: Paul Abrahimzadeh, a Partner at 1789 Capital, says stress in public-market indicators is an important guide to future private-market and IPO conditions. He points to rising credit spreads at CoreWeave, leverage and customer-concentration concerns among hyperscalers, and a CCC credit index signaling elevated default risk. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Talks Investment Landscape, Integrating AI at Schwab IMPACT
item.description: Bloomberg Businessweek examines the investment landscape from the Schwab IMPACT summit in Boston. Sam Kang, Head of Family Office and Premier Wealth Group for Schwab Advisor Services, discusses how wealthy clients approach long-term investing. Julie Sunwoo, president of DAFgiving360, discusses how the market impacts charitable giving and donor-advised funds. Plus, Rick Wurster, Schwab president and CEO, details Schwab's use of AI in investment services, while D.J. Tierney, senior investment portfolio strategist at Schwab Asset Management, and Michael Vogelzang, CIO at CAPTRUST, discuss risks from AI & tech. Kevin Gordon, Schwab head of Macro Research & Investing, discusses third-quarter GDP and how economic data differs from how people feel about the economy. Mark Mezzanotte, head of Private Wealth Solutions for iCapital, and Jalina Kerr, Schwab head of Advisor Experience, discuss the flows to alternative investments and private equity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Stocks Slide as Markets Rotate Into Small Caps
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Rockefeller Global Family Office CIO Jimmy Chang, Tradeweb CEO Billy Hult, Wedbush Managing Director, Internet Equity Research Analyst Ygal Arounian, Raymond James Financial CEO Paul Shoukry, GE Healthcare CEO Peter Arduini, Deutsche Bank Head of Asset Allocation, Chief Global Strategist Binky Chadha, Jefferies Software & Internet Research Tech Sector Leader Brent Thill, Seaport Research Partners Semiconductors & Electronics Senior Analyst Jay Goldberg, T. Rowe Price Portfolio Manager Tony Wang, Placer.ai Head of Analytical Research RJ Hottovy, 1789 Capital Partner Paul Abrahimzadeh, & New Balance President & CEO Joe Preston. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s DHS-Owned Deportation Fleet Makes First Removal Flights
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security for the first time has used one of its recently acquired planes to send deportees to Mexico, potentially ending months of uncertainty about jets bought under former Secretary Kristi Noem.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell and Siddharth Philip

item.title: Why the US Economy Feels Worse Than It Looks
item.description:
According to government data, these are good times for the US economy. Consumer spending is strong, job losses are relatively low. But by many other measures, Americans are miserable. What’s going on?
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Senate Map Brightens for Democrats While Alaska Race Gets Messier
item.description: Red states offer an unusual opening even as Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate faces controversy.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: California Leads $84B Slate of Midterm Muni Bond Measures
item.description: Bloomberg's Aashna Shah joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." State and local governments across the US are asking voters to approve at least $84 billion of bond sales next week, exceeding levels in recent elections in a push to finance infrastructure projects as well as housing affordability measures. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors, Bonds Jolted by Lula Win in Brazil
item.description: Bloomberg's Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Investors blindsided by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election are balking at buying into Brazil’s markets after bullish bets on the nation’s assets unraveled spectacularly. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lagarde's Exit, Safe Havens, Record Credit Sales
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: JPMorgan Asset Management CIO of US CFICC Kay Herr, Invesco Co-Head of Global Fixed Income Business Strategy Stephanie Larosiliere, Goldman Sachs Chief Credit Strategist Amanda Lynam, and CreditSights Global Head of Credit Strategy Winnie Cisar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alaska Senate Race: Trump Says Peltola Should Be Banned
item.description: President Donald Trump says Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola should banned from the US Senate race. The New York Times reported that Peltola and allies tried to find people with names similar to Dan Sullivan to run. Sullivan is the Republican incumbent. Tyler Kendall and Joe Mathieu discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fox News Moves South Carolina Senate Contest to Toss-Up in New Rating
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to South Carolina on Thursday to bolster incumbent Senator Darline Graham, as her race in the historic Republican stronghold was moved to a “toss-up” by Fox News.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: China Elevates Key Actor in Purges With Rare Politburo Pick
item.description: The Chinese Communist Party restocked its powerful Politburo for the first time in more than three decades and announced plans to hold a congress next year, where it’s set to unveil new leadership.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
